RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make root-cause identification easy and avoid masking failures.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if only one method call/scenario is exercised; non-compliant if multiple Act operations or multiple scenarios are present.
DECISION RULES: The method calls retiraAresta twice for different scenarios (removing absent edge then removing present edge) and asserts both behaviors in one test; therefore multiple Act operations exist -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be independent and not rely on shared mutable state.
RATIONALE: Independence allows arbitrary execution order and parallel runs.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use local variables and no shared mutable state or if proper setup/teardown is used.
DECISION RULES: This test uses only local variables (grafo0) and does not rely on shared static or instance state; no numbered test names present -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should check both happy paths and error/exception scenarios.
RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and correct handling of invalid inputs.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if for each method there exist at least two tests (happy path and error case) or explicit exception assertions.
DECISION RULES: The class contains only one test method overall. Although the method exercises an absent-edge removal (error-like), the guideline requires at least two distinct test methods covering normal and exceptional flows. With only one test method in the class, it fails the rule -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate boundary values (min, max, just outside) such as negative indices, zero, max indices.
RATIONALE: Boundaries are common sources of off-by-one and range errors.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if test data includes empty/zero/negative/MAX values or explicit boundary-named tests.
DECISION RULES: The test uses values 0 and 1957 but does not explicitly exercise minimum/maximum or values just outside valid ranges (e.g., -1, size-1) as boundary checks; no dedicated boundary tests -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained, reusable, and avoid duplication by extracting helpers/constants.
RATIONALE: Modularity reduces duplication and improves maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if helper methods or constants are used; non-compliant if magic values are repeated and no helpers exist.
DECISION RULES: The test uses several hard-coded magic values (1957, 0) and includes repeated setup inline with no private helpers or constants -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Keep test methods small (<20 lines) and avoid complexity (loops, nested conditionals).
RATIONALE: Smaller, simpler tests are easier to understand and less error-prone.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if short and linear; non-compliant if >30 lines or contains loops/conditionals.
DECISION RULES: The test method is relatively long and performs multiple logical steps (insert, test absent removal, test presence, cleanup) increasing its complexity; in combination with multiple act/assert groups, it exceeds recommended simplicity -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive and verify relevant properties.
RATIONALE: Multiple precise assertions increase fault-detection capability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if multiple properties are asserted (>=2) or collection size and content are checked.
DECISION RULES: The test checks null/non-null, existence, removed edge destination and vertex count — multiple precise assertions verifying different properties -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or commented-out tests; keep tests runnable.
RATIONALE: Disabled or commented tests hide defects and reduce confidence.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no @Ignore/@Disabled and no commented-out @Test.
DECISION RULES: Source contains no @Ignore/@Disabled and no commented-out tests -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be linked to requirements via annotations or Javadoc.
RATIONALE: Traceability aids impact analysis and ensures requirements coverage.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if class or methods have @Story/@Requirement or Javadoc with REQ IDs.
DECISION RULES: Class-level Javadoc includes 'REQ:DS-GRAPH-001' and 'REQ:DS-GRAPH-002' -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests should be explicit and separate.
RATIONALE: Non-functional requirements must be validated explicitly.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if explicit performance/timeouts or security tests are present.
DECISION RULES: The test uses @Test(timeout = 4000), an explicit timing constraint; therefore there is an explicit performance-related assertion -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome.
RATIONALE: Descriptive names make tests self-documenting.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if method names follow methodName_scenario_expected or BDD-style; non-compliant if generic names like test6.
DECISION RULES: The method name is 'test6', which is generic and does not describe scenario or expected result -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Generated test code should be minimal and intention-revealing.
RATIONALE: Heavy auto-generated tests are verbose and hard to maintain.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if signs of heavy code generation exist (auto-generated comments, EvoSuite imports, generic names like test6).
DECISION RULES: The file imports org.evosuite.runtime.* and the test name 'test6' is indicative of automated generation -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then, BDD naming) and be prioritized.
RATIONALE: Thoughtful design leads to better coverage and maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if Given-When-Then comments or BDD naming exist or multiple scenario coverage is present.
DECISION RULES: The test contains explicit Given/When/Then comments and descriptive assertion messages demonstrating design intent -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should verify public behavior and avoid internal implementation details.
RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are less brittle and easier to maintain.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests only call public APIs and do not use reflection or inspect private fields.
DECISION RULES: The test only exercises public Grafo methods (insereAresta, retiraAresta, existeAresta, numVertices) and does not use reflection -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be specific and include messages to aid diagnosis.
RATIONALE: Clear, specific assertions catch subtle faults and ease debugging.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if assertions use specific methods and include descriptive messages.
DECISION RULES: The test uses assertNull/assertTrue/assertNotNull/assertEquals with descriptive messages in most assertions -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why' and be minimal; avoid commented-out code.
RATIONALE: Good comments improve understanding without clutter.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if comments are minimal and explain intent; non-compliant if commented-out code or excessive comments present.
DECISION RULES: The test includes concise Given-When-Then comments and no commented-out code -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid non-deterministic sources like random, time, or external dependencies without mocking.
RATIONALE: Deterministic tests prevent flakiness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no Random/System.currentTimeMillis/Thread.sleep or unmocked external calls exist.
DECISION RULES: The test uses only deterministic Grafo operations and local state; no random/time/sleep/external deps present -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests must not leave persistent side effects or modify global state.
RATIONALE: Side-effect-free tests can run in any order without interference.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use local variables and clean up resources; non-compliant if files/databases are modified without cleanup.
DECISION RULES: This test creates a local Grafo and removes inserted edges within the same test; it does not modify global/static state and performs cleanup -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Use labels or categories to organize tests for selective execution.
RATIONALE: Labels enable targeted runs (e.g., unit vs integration).
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if @Tag/@Category annotations are present and meaningful.
DECISION RULES: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class) which provides classification -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.
